meta.title: About Us - Placer Forest School | Nature Education in Rocklin, Lincoln, Loomis & Roseville
meta.description: Meet the team behind Placer Forest School's nature-based education program serving families in Rocklin, Lincoln, Loomis, and Roseville, CA.

team.title: 👥 Meet Our Team
team.description: Our educators are passionate about supporting children's natural development through outdoor learning.

members.name: Gosia Liro
members.bio: Hi, I'm Gosia — a biology PhD, mother of two curious boys, and co-founder of Placer Forest School. My journey to forest education began when I stepped away from my work in science to be home with my children. That transition sparked a deep interest in child development, respectful parenting, and the role of nature in learning and emotional growth. We found an early foundation at Roseville Community Preschool, where I experienced the value of unstructured play, emotional awareness, and connection-based parenting. As I began homeschooling, nature quickly became our classroom — a place where my children could move freely, explore deeply, and grow at their own pace. Inspired by educators and researchers who advocate for child-led, nature-based learning, I started a weekly parent-child nature group. It became a space for kids to lead their own adventures — from tracking animals and studying bones to catching tadpoles in spring. That small group became the heart of our homeschool experience — and the seed for this forest school. Now, I'm excited to offer a drop-off forest program for children ages 4 to 12 years old — a much-needed option for families throughout Placer County, including Lincoln, Roseville, Loomis, and Rocklin areas. Our school supports children in building confidence, friendships, and resilience through meaningful time in nature. At Placer Forest School, we honor childhood as a time of wonder, movement, curiosity, and connection. 💬 For the full list of books and ideas that have shaped our philosophy, visit our Resource page. Let's grow a community rooted in nature, respect, and joyful discovery.

members.name: Beth Lippmann
members.bio:
Hello! I'm Beth, a lifelong nature-lover. The forest truly sings to me. I hold a master's degree in Non-Profit Management, but my greatest joy right now comes from nurturing my two adventurous young daughters and sharing with them my deep love for the outdoors. We are so lucky to live in the Sacramento Valley surrounded by incredible natural beauty - right in our own backyard. My passion is helping others connect with that beauty too.

I have always dreamed to share my knowledge and love of the natural world with children. I attended many of Gosia's inspiring weekly meetups in our nature explorers group for families. She began to share her vision with me… a forest school. A place where children could learn, explore, and thrive in nature. My heart soared for her, and I'm happy to share this opportunity to serve your child.

You'll often find me with my kids covered in dirt… or muddy creek water. Dirt does not hurt. Kids should be encouraged to dig, climb, and wonder. I believe that through hands-on experiences, children develop a deeper understanding of how the world works, while also learning resilience, teamwork, and problem-solving. Most importantly, they get the freedom to play, discover, and grow at their own pace.

At forest school, mess is welcomed and curiosity is celebrated.

One of my favorite sayings is "You cannot bounce off the walls if you remove the walls" by Erin Kenny. Forest school removes those walls, literally and figuratively. When children are free from the confines of a classroom, they flourish. I believe a child builds essential life skills by cooperating with peers, testing their boundaries safely, and learning directly from the natural world around them.

As John Lubbock wrote, "Earth and sky, woods and fields, lakes and rivers, the mountain and the sea, are excellent schoolmasters, and teach some of us more than we can ever learn from books."

I look forward to meeting your child and invite your family to step outside, take down the walls, and watch your child grow in wonder.
